speaker: Unknown
en: So there I was, 39 years old, and essentially hearing, here's $10 million and your history.
zh: 于是我就在那里，39 岁，基本上听到的就是：这是 1000 万美元，还有你的历史。

speaker: Unknown
en: John Gutfried, managing partner of Wall Street's hottest firm, told me that my life as Salomon Brothers was finished.
zh: John Gutfried，华尔街最热门公司的管理合伙人，告诉我在所罗门兄弟公司的人生已经结束了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's time for you to leave, he said.
zh: 他说，该是你离开的时候了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was terminated from the only full-time job I'd ever known and from the high-pressure life that I loved.
zh: 我从我唯一知道的全职工作、从我热爱的那种高压生活中被解雇了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This, after 15 years of 12-hour days and six-day weeks.
zh: 这是在 15 年的每天 12 小时、每周工作 6 天之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: Out.
zh: 走人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fired.
zh: 被解雇了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of the 63 partners were asked to stay on as employees of the new company.
zh: 63 个合伙人中的大多数被要求留任，成为新公司的雇员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not me, though, and a half a dozen other guys were pushed out at that time as well.
zh: 但我不是，当时还有另外五六个人也被踢了出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was I sad on the drive home?
zh: 开车回家的路上我难过吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You bet.
zh: 那当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as usual, I was much too macho to show it.
zh: 但和往常一样，我太过逞强，不会表现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I did have $10 million as compensation for my hurt feelings.
zh: 而且我确实拿到了 1000 万美元，作为对我受伤感情的补偿。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they had said, we had another job for you, I'd have done it in a second.
zh: 如果他们说，我们还有一份工作给你，我会立刻接受。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just as I did at an earlier career turning point in 1979 when Billy and John told me to give up my sales and trading responsibilities and supervise the computer systems area.
zh: 就像 1979 年早先的一个职业转折点一样，当时 Billy 和 John 让我放弃销售和交易的职责，去监管计算机系统部门。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was willing to do anything that they wanted.
zh: 只要他们想要，我什么都愿意做。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a great organization and I would have been happy to stay.
zh: 那是一个很棒的组织，我很乐意留下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would have never left voluntarily.
zh: 我绝不会主动离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: Afterward, I didn't sit around wondering what was happening at the old firm.
zh: 之后，我没有闲坐着琢磨老东家那边发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't go back and visit.
zh: 我没有回去看看。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never look over my shoulder.
zh: 我从不回头看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once finished, gone.
zh: 一旦结束，就结束。

speaker: Unknown
en: Life continues.
zh: 生活继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that is from the beginning of the book that we talked about today, which is the autobiography of Michael Bloomberg.
zh: 这就是我们今天聊的这本书的开头，也就是 Michael Bloomberg 的自传。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is called Bloomberg by Bloomberg, and he's describing the fact that getting fired was one of the best things that ever happened to him.
zh: 书名叫《Bloomberg by Bloomberg》，他描述的是被解雇这件事其实是他人生中遇到的最好的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a great line by Steve Jobs that comes to mind where he says that sometimes life is going to hit you in the head with a brick, but don't lose faith.
zh: 我想起 Steve Jobs 的一句名言，他说有时候生活会用一块砖砸你的脑袋，但不要失去信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Bloomberg said, I didn't look back.
zh: 所以 Bloomberg 说，我没有回头。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was going to take the $10 million that he got from the sale of the company and jump right back into the arena, this time as an entrepreneur.
zh: 他打算拿着从公司出售中得到的 1000 万美元，立刻跳回竞技场，这一次是以创业者的身份。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Bloomberg grew up working class.
zh: Bloomberg 是工薪阶层家庭出身的。

speaker: Unknown
en: His parents didn't have a lot of money.
zh: 他的父母没有很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to skip over childhood.
zh: 我要跳过童年部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to go right into when he went to Harvard Business School.
zh: 我想直接讲到他上哈佛商学院的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is right at the end of Harvard.
zh: 这是在哈佛快结束的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really, he's not sure what to do after college.
zh: 说真的，他还不确定大学毕业后要做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, my two years at Harvard were well spent.
zh: 他说，我在哈佛的两年过得很有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Harvard's case method teaching honed my analytical skills and sharpened my communication abilities.
zh: 哈佛的案例教学法磨炼了我的分析能力，也锐化了我的沟通能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: The academic standards there were superior, but not what I would call outstanding.
zh: 那里的学术水准很优秀，但我不会称之为杰出。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were some very bright students in my class, some classmates I thought not exactly intellectually gifted, and a few that I considered total frauds who could only talk a good game.
zh: 我班上有一些非常聪明的学生，也有一些同学我认为算不上有天赋，还有少数几个我认为是彻头彻尾的骗子，只会耍嘴皮子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those who I thought were smart generally did well later in life.
zh: 那些我认为聪明的人，后来在人生中普遍干得不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those who I considered dummies did less well.
zh: 那些我认为是笨蛋的人，干得就没那么好。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bullshitters faded away.
zh: 那些吹牛的人逐渐消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Street smarts and common sense, it turned out, were better predictors of career achievements.
zh: 事实证明，街头智慧和常识是职业成就更好的预测指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: By this point, I hadn't really pondered where my life and work would take me.
zh: 到这个时候，我还没有真正思考过我的人生和工作会把我带向何方。

speaker: Unknown
en: What should I do with my life?
zh: 我该用我的人生做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I talked to my good friend, Steve.
zh: 我和我好友 Steve 聊了聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Steve told me to call the firms of Salomon Brothers and Goldman Sachs to say that I was desperate to be an institutional salesperson or an equity trader.
zh: Steve 让我打电话给 Salomon Brothers 和 Goldman Sachs，说我急切地想成为一名机构销售或股票交易员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who are they, meaning who is Goldman Sachs and who is Salomon Brothers, and what would I be doing?
zh: 他们是谁，意思是 Goldman Sachs 是谁、Salomon Brothers 是谁，以及我会做什么工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't worry about it, Steve told me.
zh: 别操心这个，Steve 告诉我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just do it.
zh: 照做就是了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not having any better ideas of my own, I made the calls.
zh: 我自己也没有更好的主意，就打了电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he makes the point that these jobs at the time were considered very like low status.
zh: 然后他指出,这些工作在当时被认为是地位很低的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says security trading and sales were considered second class occupations in those days.
zh: 他说,证券交易和销售在那个时候被认为是二等职业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both involved getting your hands dirty by actually picking up the telephone and talking to customers.
zh: 两者都需要弄脏双手,真的拿起电话和客户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: So essentially what he's describing at this point in his life and this point in this book.
zh: 所以本质上,他在书的这个节点、在他人生的这个节点所描述的,

speaker: Unknown
en: Essentially, he's learning the meta skill of sales.
zh: 本质上,他是在学习销售这门元技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did this episode of Ken Griffin, I think last year, maybe the year before.
zh: 我做 Ken Griffin 那期节目,我记得是去年,也可能是前年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when one of Ken Griffin's mentors retired, he said, hey, come to my office, you can grab anything that you want.
zh: 当 Ken Griffin 的一位导师退休时,他说,嘿,来我办公室,你可以随便拿任何你想要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I thought was interesting is Ken wanted this like $10 sign, this plaque that was in his mentor's office that said, if we're going to eat, someone's got to sell.
zh: 我觉得有意思的是,Ken 想要的是导师办公室里一块大约 10 美元的牌子,上面写着:如果我们要吃饭,就得有人去卖。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then
zh: 然后

speaker: Unknown
en: In that episode, Ken was giving advice to college students and he says, you're always selling and if you don't like to sell, here's my advice, get over it.
zh: 在那期节目里,Ken 在给大学生建议时说,你总是在卖东西,如果你不喜欢卖,这是我的建议:克服它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Michael Bloomberg would agree with what Ken Griffin was saying, talks a lot about the importance of selling and that this point in his life was hugely beneficial in the future decades of him building his own company.
zh: 我觉得 Michael Bloomberg 会同意 Ken Griffin 的话,他谈了很多销售的重要性,而他人生中的这个节点对他之后几十年建立自己的公司大有裨益。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most valuable privately held companies in the world, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一句,那是世界上最有价值的私人持有公司之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both involve getting your hands dirty by actually picking up the telephone and talking to customers.
zh: 两者都需要弄脏双手,真的拿起电话和客户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Forget the fact that almost all occupations have a big selling component.
zh: 先别管几乎所有职业都有很大的销售成分这一事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to sell your firm, your ideas, and yourself.
zh: 你必须推销你的公司、你的想法,以及你自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: Overlook the fact that a good trading mentality is synonymous with the ability and discipline to compartmentalize, focus, and compete for success.
zh: 先别管一个良好的交易心态与分割事务、专注以及为成功竞争的能力和纪律是同义词这一事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: In those days, no self-respecting research analyst or banker ever thought of working the phones, of actually bringing in business.
zh: 在那些日子里,没有自尊的研究分析师或银行家会想过要打电话、真正去拉业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: They thought soliciting was undignified.
zh: 他们认为招揽业务有失身份。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is the first few years of his company.
zh: 而这是他公司成立的最初几年。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was probably the best salesperson of Bloomberg when he starts it.
zh: 他创办 Bloomberg 时,可能是公司里最好的销售员。

speaker: Unknown
en: For me, with college loans to pay off, a good job was a good job.
zh: 对我来说,还有大学贷款要还,一份好工作就是一份好工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I would learn later in life, it's the doers, the lean and hungry ones, those with ambition in their eyes and fire in their bellies, who go the furthest and achieve the most.
zh: 正如我后来在人生中学到的,是那些实干家,那些精瘦而饥饿的人,那些眼里有野心、腹中有火焰的人,走得最远、成就最大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I absolutely love this part because he winds up getting an offer from both Goldman Sachs and Solomon Brothers.
zh: 所以我绝对喜欢这一部分,因为他最后同时拿到了 Goldman Sachs 和 Solomon Brothers 的录用通知。

speaker: Unknown
en: Goldman offers him $14,000 a year.
zh: Goldman 给他开了一年 14,000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Solomon offers him $9,000.
zh: Solomon 给他 9,000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he wanted to take the job at Solomon.
zh: 所以他想去 Solomon 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's like, I literally would starve.
zh: 他意思是,我真的会饿死。

speaker: Unknown
en: I cannot live on $9,000.
zh: 我没法靠 9,000 美元生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have no money.
zh: 我没有钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have student debt.
zh: 我有学生贷款。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm in New York City.
zh: 我在纽约市。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so essentially this is his financial situation at the beginning of his career.
zh: 所以本质上,这就是他职业生涯开始时的财务状况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I cannot afford to work at Solomon.
zh: 你看,我负担不起去 Solomon 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's talking to Guthrie.
zh: 于是他在和 Guthrie 谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the same guy that's going to fire him many years later.
zh: 这就是多年后要解雇他的那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to, I love it, but I don't own another suit of clothes.
zh: 我想要,我喜欢这份工作,但我没有另一套衣服。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have an apartment to live in.
zh: 我没有公寓可住。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have no cash in the bank.
zh: 我银行里没有现金。

speaker: Unknown
en: All I've got are outstanding student loans that I took for tuition when the part-time campus job as a school parking lot attendant didn't pay enough.
zh: 我有的只是为学费借的未还学生贷款,因为学校停车场管理员的兼职校园工作挣得不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he's asked how much you need.
zh: 于是他被问到需要多少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, I need $11,500.
zh: 他说,我需要 11,500 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So remember, they offered him $9,000 a year.
zh: 记住,他们给他开的年薪是 9,000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, fine, that's $9,000 salary and I'll give you a $2,500 loan.
zh: 他说,好,那就是 9,000 美元薪水,我再借给你 2,500 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he talks about the culture at Solomon Brothers.
zh: 于是他谈到 Solomon Brothers 的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, to say that I fit into Solomon and love the industry is an understatement.
zh: 他说,说我融入了 Solomon 并热爱这个行业,都算是轻描淡写。

speaker: Unknown
en: I reveled in it every minute of the day.
zh: 我每天每一分钟都乐在其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: The year is 1966 and Michael Bloomberg is 24 years old and he talks about the difference in leadership between the two different people that are gonna run the firm.
zh: 那一年是 1966 年,Michael Bloomberg 24 岁,他谈到将要运营这家公司的两个不同人之间领导力的差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: He absolutely loved Billy Salomon.
zh: 他绝对热爱 Billy Salomon。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, the boss when I joined was Billy Salomon.
zh: 他说,我加入时的老板是 Billy Salomon。

speaker: Unknown
en: Billy made the culture special.
zh: Billy 让这种文化变得特别。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was decisive and consistent as a leader.
zh: 作为领导者，他果断且始终如一。

speaker: Unknown
en: If he ever harbored doubts after making a decision, I never saw it.
zh: 即使他做出决定后内心有过疑虑，我也从未看出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was easily approachable and willing to listen to everyone's views.
zh: 他平易近人，愿意倾听每个人的意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: When he said we were going left, we went left.
zh: 当他说我们往左走，我们就往左走。

speaker: Unknown
en: When he said right, right it was.
zh: 当他说往右，那就往右。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have to prepare for both directions.
zh: 我们不必为两个方向都做准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: He set the rules.
zh: 他制定规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was no different set of rules for him.
zh: 对他自己没有任何另一套规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: He led by example.
zh: 他以身作则。

speaker: Unknown
en: What he said, he did, and the rest of us did as well.
zh: 他说到做到，我们其他人也照着做。

speaker: Unknown
en: John was a great leader too, but I always thought that he listened to too many people.
zh: John 也是一位伟大的领导者，但我一直觉得他听了太多人的意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: It made running the firm much more difficult for him.
zh: 这使得他管理公司要困难得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Smart people prepared for both left and right when John succeeded Billy.
zh: 当 John 接替 Billy 时，聪明人会同时为向左和向右做准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: This event split resources and made it harder to lead when the going got tough.
zh: 这件事分散了资源，使得情况变得艰难时更难领导。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unlike Billy, John consulted all interested parties before making a decision.
zh: 与 Billy 不同，John 在做决定前会咨询所有相关方。

speaker: Unknown
en: No matter how noble the motive, that resulted in indecisiveness.
zh: 无论动机多么高尚，这都导致了优柔寡断。

speaker: Unknown
en: Comparing John to Billy on leadership, I always thought John was more egalitarian but less effective.
zh: 在领导力方面把 John 和 Billy 相比，我一直觉得 John 更讲平等但效率更低。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he starts out at the very bottom.
zh: 所以他从最底层开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, he has to work in his underwear in an unconditioned bank vault.
zh: 事实上，他不得不只穿着内衣在一间没有空调的银行金库里工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is hilarious.
zh: 这太搞笑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Remember, it's 1966.
zh: 记住，那是 1966 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked my first summer there in the cage.
zh: 我第一个夏天在那里是在笼子里工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were physically counting securities by hand.
zh: 我们在用手清点证券。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a pretty lowly start.
zh: 这是一个相当低微的起点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We slaved in our underwear in an unair-conditioned bank vault with an occasional six-pack of beer to make it more bearable.
zh: 我们穿着内衣在没有空调的银行金库里苦干，偶尔来一提六罐装啤酒让自己好受一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he reinforces the low status nature of the job that he chose, the one that he had.
zh: 然后他强调了这份他所选择的、他所拥有的工作的低微性质。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had no other way to feed himself.
zh: 他没有其他办法养活自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's really too embarrassed to tell his friends who at the time were much more successful than he was.
zh: 而且他真的羞于告诉他的朋友们，当时他们比他成功得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: My friends asked what I was doing for work.
zh: 我的朋友们问我在做什么工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: To save face, I told them I was studying methods and procedures to simplify workflows.
zh: 为了保住面子，我告诉他们我在研究简化工序和流程的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: My friends were research analysts and investment bankers with lush private offices.
zh: 我的朋友们是研究分析师和投资银行家，拥有豪华的私人办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was what can only be called a clerk.
zh: 而我只配被称作一个职员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why didn't I quit?
zh: 我为什么不辞职？

speaker: Unknown
en: I was too embarrassed.
zh: 我太难为情了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then again, this was great preparation for his future career.
zh: 再者，这是对他未来职业生涯的极好锻炼。

speaker: Unknown
en: He talks a lot about sales in the book.
zh: 他在书里谈了很多关于销售的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's going to give us basically this definition of what he considers a good sales technique.
zh: 他基本上会给我们一个他认为是好的销售技巧的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did what all great salespeople do.
zh: 我们做了所有伟大的销售员都会做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We presented everything we had and then highlighted whatever facts enabled customers to convince themselves that they were getting a good deal.
zh: 我们展示我们所拥有的一切，然后突出任何能让客户说服自己他们正在做成一笔好买卖的事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he's selling securities over the phone.
zh: 于是他通过电话销售证券。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both of his bosses are watching him.
zh: 他的两个老板都在看着他。

speaker: Unknown
en: It says, Billy and John would stand over me, watching silently while I was on the phone with a customer, head down, totally focused on making the sale, talking, explaining, cajoling, pleading.
zh: 书里写道，Billy 和 John 会站在我身边，沉默地看着我打电话给客户，低着头，全神贯注于做成这单生意，说着、解释着、劝诱着、恳求着。

speaker: Unknown
en: I felt a great thrill when I closed the deal.
zh: 当我谈成交易时，我感到一阵巨大的兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: After I closed the deal, they would walk away without a word.
zh: 我谈成交易后，他们会一言不发地走开。

speaker: Unknown
en: There weren't any congratulations.
zh: 没有任何祝贺。

speaker: Unknown
en: They weren't needed.
zh: 也不需要祝贺。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was expected to make big trades.
zh: 做成大单是我分内的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we get back into this, I want to tell you about the presenting sponsor of this podcast, Ramp.
zh: 在我们继续之前，我想告诉你本播客的首席赞助商 Ramp。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have been reading a lot about SpaceX lately.
zh: 我最近读了很多关于 SpaceX 的资料。

speaker: Unknown
en: SpaceX is one of the most valuable businesses in the world, and one of the main themes in the history of SpaceX is constantly attacking and questioning your cost.
zh: SpaceX 是世界上最有价值的公司之一，而 SpaceX 历史上的一个主要主题就是不断攻击和质疑你的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: RAMP helps many of the most innovative businesses in the world do exactly that.
zh: RAMP 帮助世界上许多最具创新性的企业做到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they do this by using first principles thinking.
zh: 他们通过第一性原理思维来实现这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The median company running on RAMP cuts their expenses by 5%.
zh: 在 RAMP 上运营的公司中位数公司削减了 5% 的开支。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing that SpaceX has demonstrated is that a religious dedication to controlling your costs helps increase revenue because you can pursue opportunities you couldn't otherwise.
zh: SpaceX 已经证明的一件事是，对控制成本的执着投入有助于增加收入，因为你可以追求原本无法追求的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we see that in the RAMP data too.
zh: 我们在 RAMP 的数据中也看到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The median company running on RAMP also grows their revenue by 16%.
zh: 在 RAMP 上运营的公司中位数公司收入也增长了 16%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you're running your business on RAMP and your competitors are not, you have a massive competitive advantage that compounds over time.
zh: 所以当你在 RAMP 上运营你的业务而你的竞争对手没有时，你就拥有了一个随时间复利的巨大竞争优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: RAMP is the only platform designed to make your finance team faster and happier.
zh: RAMP 是唯一一个旨在让你的财务团队更快、更开心的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of the top founders and CEOs that I know run their business on RAMP.
zh: 我认识的许多顶尖创始人和 CEO 都在 RAMP 上运营他们的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I run my business on RAMP and you should too.
zh: 我在 RAMP 上运营我的业务，你也应该这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to RAMP.com today to learn how they can help your business save time.
zh: 今天就去 RAMP.com 了解他们如何帮助你的企业节省时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Save money and grow revenue.
zh: 节省资金并增长收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is ramp.com.
zh: 那就是 ramp.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so even though he's going to make his first small fortune in finance, he never thought if he was going to be an entrepreneur that he would be an entrepreneur in finance.
zh: 所以即使他将在金融领域赚到他的第一笔小财富，他从未想过如果他要成为企业家的话，他会成为金融领域的企业家。

speaker: Unknown
en: He wanted to actually have a real business that had a real service that made real people's lives better.
zh: 他实际上想要拥有一个真正的企业，提供真正的服务，让真正的人们的生活变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he has this, I skipped over this part in his childhood and then also in high school and college, he has this love of history.
zh: 然后他还有这个——我跳过了他童年时期的这一部分，还有高中和大学时期——他热爱历史。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's constantly
zh: 所以他不断地——

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he says, Wall Street promised vast riches, although a few of the great fortunes had been made there.
zh: 所以他说，华尔街承诺了巨大的财富，尽管只有少数巨大的财富是在那里赚到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: From John D. Rockefeller to Sam Walton to Bill Gates, great financial success comes from starting businesses with concrete products in the real world, building jobs, creating value, and helping people.
zh: 从约翰·D·洛克菲勒到山姆·沃尔顿再到比尔·盖茨，巨大的财务成功来自于在现实世界中创办拥有具体产品的企业，创造就业机会，创造价值，并帮助人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are not yet in the story, though, where he starts Bloomberg.
zh: 不过，我们还没有讲到他创办 Bloomberg 的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's still telling us essentially lessons that he learned at Salomon Brothers that he would use when he built his own company.
zh: 他基本上还在告诉我们他在 Salomon Brothers 学到的经验教训，这些他会在建立自己的公司时用到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now this is in 1967.
zh: 所以现在是 1967 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a year after he starts working at Salomon Brothers.
zh: 这是他开始在 Salomon Brothers 工作一年之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, didn't grow up with money.
zh: 再说一次，他不是在有钱人家长大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now he's exposed to people that have a lot of money and it's
zh: 现在他接触到了有很多钱的人，而且——

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just kind of like humorous and funny stories about, you know, him peeking into this world that he didn't even know existed.
zh: 就是那种挺幽默有趣的关于他窥探这个他甚至不知道存在的世界的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, fast forward to this day, you know, he's rumored to be, you know, one of, if not the wealthiest person in America.
zh: 现在，快进到今天，你知道，传闻他是美国最富有的人之一，如果不是最富有的那个的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard a bunch of different stories about this, that he essentially been pulling out billions and billions in dividends out of his company for, you know, more than two decades.
zh: 我听说过关于这件事的很多不同说法，说他基本上二十多年来一直在从他的公司里拿出数十亿又数十亿的股息。

speaker: Unknown
en: But back at this point in the story, he's in his early 20s, mid 20s, and he's going to a fancy dinner at a very nice New York restaurant.
zh: 但回到故事的这个时点，他二十岁出头，二十五六岁，他要去一家非常好的纽约餐厅参加一场高档晚宴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he says, I couldn't stop gawking.
zh: 他说，我禁不住目瞪口呆。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was my first time in such opulent surroundings.
zh: 那是我第一次置身如此奢华的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's talking about the person that's sitting next to him.
zh: 他说的是坐在他旁边的那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he says, her topics of conversation were equally incomprehensible.
zh: 他说，她谈话的话题也同样令人难以理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: She asked, where did my family have vacation houses in Europe?
zh: 她问，我们家在欧洲的度假别墅在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: In what country was our yacht registered?
zh: 我们的游艇注册在哪个国家？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do we keep our plane?
zh: 我们的飞机停放在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: My late father, who never earned more than $6,000 per year, would have chuckled.
zh: 我已故的父亲，他每年收入从不超过 6000 美元，要是听到会莞尔一笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: In front of me was more silverware per place setting than my family owned in total.
zh: 在我面前的每一套餐位上的银餐具，比我全家拥有的总数还要多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought I'd gone through the looking glass into another world.
zh: 我以为自己穿过了镜子进入了另一个世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so early in his career, he has a really great idea where he's like, okay, Billy's the boss.
zh: 所以在他职业生涯早期，他有一个非常好的想法，就是：好，Billy 是老板。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to make myself indispensable to the boss.
zh: 我要让自己对老板来说是不可或缺的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, keep in mind, this is his first, second year that he's working there.
zh: 记住，这是他在那里工作的第一、第二年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say 14, 15 years in the future, he's going to wind up getting $10 million and then fired from this job.
zh: 比方说 14、15 年之后的将来，他最终会从这份工作中拿到 1000 万美元然后被解雇。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this, he would have never got the $10 million and then, therefore, the seed capital he needed to start Bloomberg, this, you know, this very valuable business that he still owns today, if it wasn't for the things that he's doing at this point in his career.
zh: 但是，如果不是因为他在职业生涯这个时点所做的事情，他永远不可能拿到那 1000 万美元，因此也不可能拿到他创办 Bloomberg 所需要的种子资金——这家非常有价值的公司，他至今仍然拥有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, the great thing about this book is, one, it's very simple language.
zh: 而且他说，这本书的伟大之处在于，第一，它的语言非常简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bloomberg is unapologetically extreme and he's also very, very direct.
zh: Bloomberg 毫不道歉地极端，而且他也非常非常直接。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he'll tell you a story and he's like, I don't know, this seems like obvious, everybody should just do this.
zh: 所以他会给你讲一个故事，然后说，我不知道，这看起来很明显，每个人都应该就这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the moral of the story he's about to tell us is if you have a job and you have a boss, why aren't you automatically making yourself indispensable?
zh: 而他即将给我们讲的这个故事的寓意是：如果你有一份工作，你有一个老板，你为什么不自动地让自己变得不可或缺呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the fastest way to move up.
zh: 这是最快的晋升方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came in every morning at 7 a.m. getting there before everyone else except Billy.
zh: 我每天早上 7 点就到，比除 Billy 之外的所有人都早到。

speaker: Unknown
en: When he needed to borrow a match or talk sports, I was the only other person in the trading room, so he talked to me.
zh: 当他需要借根火柴或者聊聊体育时，我是交易室里唯一的另一个人，所以他就跟我说话。

speaker: Unknown
en: At age 26, I became a buddy of the managing partner.
zh: 26 岁时，我成了管理合伙人的哥们儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would stay later than anyone else when he needed someone to make an after-hours call to a big client.
zh: 当他需要有人在下班后给大客户打电话时，我会比其他任何人都待得更晚。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or someone to listen to his complaints about those who had already gone home.
zh: 或者需要有人听他抱怨那些已经回家的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was that someone.
zh: 我就是那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Making myself omnipresent wasn't exactly burdensome.
zh: 让自己无处不在并不算什么负担。

speaker: Unknown
en: I loved what I was doing.
zh: 我热爱我正在做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And developing a close working relationship with those who ran the show probably didn't hurt my career either.
zh: 而且和掌权者建立密切的工作关系，大概对我的职业生涯也没有坏处。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never understood why everybody else doesn't do the same thing.
zh: 我一直不明白为什么其他人不这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make himself indispensable on the job.
zh: 你无法选择你起步时拥有的优势，你当然也无法挑选你的基因智力水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was exactly what I did.
zh: 那正是我所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then this is one of my favorite parts in the book.
zh: 然后这是书中我最喜欢的部分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: This part is absolutely amazing.
zh: 这部分实在太精彩了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just going to read huge chunks of the book to you from here.
zh: 从这里开始，我打算给你们大段大段地读这本书。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really on the importance of showing up, working hard, staying flexible, and then loving what you do.
zh: 它讲的是露面、努力工作、保持灵活、然后热爱你所做的事的重要性。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a handful of ideas that Bloomberg repeats throughout this entire book.
zh: 有一些理念是 Bloomberg 在整本书中反复提及的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is said that 80% of life is just showing up.
zh: 人们说，人生的 80% 就在于露面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe that.
zh: 我相信这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can never have complete mastery over your existence.
zh: 你永远无法完全掌控你的存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't choose the advantages you start out with, and you certainly can't pick your genetic intelligence level.
zh: 你无法选择自己起点拥有的优势，也肯定无法挑选自己的基因智力水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you can control how hard you work.
zh: 但你可以控制你有多努力工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure someone, someplace, is smart enough to succeed while keeping it all in perspective and not working too hard.
zh: 我相信某个地方有某个人，聪明到能够在保持全局观、不过度工作的情况下取得成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I've never met him or her.
zh: 但我从未遇到过他或她。

speaker: Unknown
en: The more you work, the better you do.
zh: 你工作得越多，你就做得越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's that simple.
zh: 就是这么简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've always outworked the other person.
zh: 我一向比对方更拼命工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I hadn't, he or she would be writing this book.
zh: 如果我没有，那么写这本书的就会是他或她。

speaker: Unknown
en: Still, I had a life.
zh: 尽管如此，我也有自己的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't remember being so driven or focused that my job got in the way of playing in the evenings and on weekends.
zh: 我不记得自己曾经-driven 到让工作妨碍了晚上和周末的玩乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: I dated a lot.
zh: 我约会过很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I skied and I jogged and I hit the town more than most other people.
zh: 我滑雪、慢跑，去城里玩得比大多数其他人都多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The more you try to do, the more life you'll have.
zh: 你尝试做的事越多，你拥有的人生就越丰富。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although I was serious about my career, I never had a budget for my future.
zh: 虽然我对我的职业很认真，但我从未为我的未来做过预算。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unlike so many of my classmates, I didn't set out to be a partner or vice president at age 30 or a trillionaire at 35.
zh: 和我的许多同学不同，我没有立誓要在 30 岁当上合伙人或副总裁，或者在 35 岁成为万亿富翁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make a comprehensive scheme for the rest of my life?
zh: 为我的余生制定一个全面的计划？

speaker: Unknown
en: I had trouble filling out the part of the college application where you're asked to write 1,500 meaningless words about what you're going to do for the next 10 years.
zh: 我连大学申请表中那道题都填不下去——要求你用 1500 个毫无意义的字写你未来 10 年要做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both at business and at home, I've never let planning get in the way of doing.
zh: 无论在工作中还是在家里，我从不让计划妨碍行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Life, I've found, works in the following way.
zh: 我发现，人生是以下面这种方式运转的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Daily, you're presented with many small and surprising opportunities.
zh: 每天，你都会面对许多微小而意外的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes you seize one that takes you to the top.
zh: 有时你抓住其中一个，它把你带到顶峰。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most, though, if valuable at all, take you only a little way.
zh: 但大多数时候，即便有价值，也只带你走一小段路。

speaker: Unknown
en: To succeed, you must string together many small incremental advances rather than count on hitting the lottery jackpot once.
zh: 要成功，你必须把许多微小的渐进式进步串联起来，而不是指望中一次彩票头奖。

speaker: Unknown
en: Trusting to great luck is a strategy not likely to work for most people.
zh: 指望极大的好运，这个策略对大多数人来说不太可能奏效。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a practical matter, constantly enhance your skills, put in as many hours as possible, and make tactical plans for the next few steps.
zh: 从实际出发，不断提升你的技能，投入尽可能多的时间，并为接下来的几步做战术性计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, based on what actually occurs, look one more move ahead and adjust the plan.
zh: 然后，根据实际发生的情况，再多看一步棋，并调整计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take lots of chances and make lots of individual spur-of-the-moment decisions.
zh: 抓住大量机会，做出大量个别的、一时兴起的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't, this is such a great line.
zh: 不要——这句台词太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't devise a five-year plan or a great leap forward.
zh: 不要制定什么五年计划或者大跃进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Central planning didn't work for Stalin or Mao and it won't work for an entrepreneur either.
zh: 中央计划对斯大林和毛泽东都行不通，对创业者同样行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every significant advance I or my company's ever made has been evolutionary rather than revolutionary.
zh: 我或我的公司所取得的每一项重大进步，都是演进而非革命性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Small earned steps, not big lucky hits.
zh: 小步稳扎稳打，而不是靠大运气的侥幸命中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I stay flexible.
zh: 我保持灵活。

speaker: Unknown
en: A reporter asked me what we at Bloomberg had failed at.
zh: 一位记者问我，我们彭博的人失败过什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: My answer after some thought was nothing, but what we accomplished wasn't always what we set out to do.
zh: 我想了想后的回答是：什么都没有，但我们所成就的并不总是我们当初想做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often in the process, things worked that we hadn't planned on.
zh: 在过程中，常常是一些我们没计划到的事情成功了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unforeseen uses arose for our products, customers appeared whom we hadn't known existed, and exactly the reverse occurred for those I had been dead sure of.
zh: 我们的产品出现了 unforeseen 的用途，出现了我们根本不知道存在的客户，而恰恰相反的情况发生在我曾经非常笃定的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Planning has its place.
zh: 规划有其位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: The actual thought process sometimes leads to great new ideas, but you can only accomplish what's possible when you get there.
zh: 实际的思考过程有时会带来很棒的新想法，但只有当你到达那里时，你才能完成可能实现的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, whatever your idea is, you've got to do more of it than anyone else, a task that's easier if you structure things so that you like doing them, since doing more almost always leads to greater accomplishments.
zh: 然后，无论你的想法是什么，你都必须比任何人都做得更多，如果你把事情安排成你喜欢做的样子，这项任务会更容易，因为做得更多几乎总会带来更大的成就。

speaker: Unknown
en: In turn, you'll have more fun, and then you'll want to do even more because of the rewards, and so on.
zh: 反过来，你会获得更多乐趣，然后因为回报你会想做得更多，如此循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've always loved my work and put in a lot of time, which has helped make me successful.
zh: 我一直热爱我的工作，投入了大量时间，这帮助我获得了成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: I truly pity people who don't like their jobs.
zh: 我真心同情那些不喜欢自己工作的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They struggle at work so unhappily for ultimately so much less success and thus develop even more reason to hate their occupations.
zh: 他们在工作中苦苦挣扎，如此不快乐，最终却只获得少得多的成功，从而又生出更多憎恨自己职业的理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's too much delightful stuff to do in this short lifetime not to love getting up on a weekday morning.
zh: 在这短暂的一生中，有太多令人愉悦的事情可做，没有理由不爱上周工作日的早晨。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he brings the story to after he got fired and starting Bloomberg.
zh: 然后他把故事带到他被解雇并创办彭博之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I've said this a few times, I think Bloomberg is unapologetically extreme.
zh: 再说一次，我说过好几次了，我认为彭博毫不掩饰地极端。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you see that right here in this paragraph.
zh: 你就在这一段里看到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, did I want to risk an embarrassing and costly failure?
zh: 他说，我想冒一个令人难堪且代价高昂的失败的风险吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 当然想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Happiness for me has always been the thrill of the unknown.
zh: 对我来说，幸福一直是未知带来的刺激。

speaker: Unknown
en: Trying something that everyone says can't be done.
zh: 尝试所有人都说做不到的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Feeling that gnawing put in my stomach that says danger ahead.
zh: 感受胃里那种咬噬般的感觉，它在说前方有危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want action.
zh: 我要行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want challenge.
zh: 我要挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Work was, is, and always will be a very big part of my life.
zh: 工作曾经是、现在是、并将永远是我生活中非常大的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love it.
zh: 我热爱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even today, after toiling for 50 years, I wake up looking forward to getting in early, practicing my profession, creating something, and competing against the best.
zh: 即使在今天，在苦干了 50 年之后，我早上醒来仍然期待着早早上班，践行我的职业，创造一些东西，并与最优秀的人竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a real high to be a participant rather than a spectator.
zh: 做一个参与者而不是旁观者，是一种真正的高潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about the percentage of your life spent working.
zh: 想想你一生中花在工作上的比例。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're not content doing it, you're probably pretty miserable with the situation.
zh: 如果你做这份工作并不满足，你可能对这种处境相当痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: Change it.
zh: 改变它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the advice that gives to start a company is think about what you do better than anyone else.
zh: 然后他给出的创业建议是：想想你比任何人都做得更好的是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would start a company that would help financial organizations.
zh: 我会创办一家帮助金融组织的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were better traders and salespeople.
zh: 有更好的交易员和销售人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were better managers and computer experts, but nobody had more knowledge of the securities and investment industries and of how technology could help them.
zh: 有更好的管理者 和计算机专家，但没有人对证券和投资行业以及技术如何能帮助这些行业有更多的了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to create something that would make smart investors out of mediocre ones and would create a competitive advantage over anyone lacking these capabilities.
zh: 我想创造一种东西，能把平庸的投资者变成聪明的投资者，并对任何缺乏这些能力的人形成竞争优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he goes back to this thing that he repeats.
zh: 然后他又回到他反复强调的那件事上。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's like, stop overanalyzing.
zh: 他说，别过度分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stop planning too much.
zh: 别规划太多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just start.
zh: 直接开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're going to succeed, you need a vision, one that's affordable, practical, and fills a customer need.
zh: 如果你要成功，你需要一个愿景，一个负担得起、切实可行、并满足客户需求的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then go for it.
zh: 然后放手去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't worry too much about the details.
zh: 不要太担心细节。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do not second guess your creativity.
zh: 不要对你的创造力进行二次猜测。

speaker: Unknown
en: Avoid overanalyzing your new project's potential.
zh: 避免过度分析你新项目的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he talks about the people stay away from.
zh: 然后他谈到要远离的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: He talks a lot of shit about bankers and venture capitalists in the book.
zh: 他在书里对银行家和风险资本家骂了不少。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he says, banks and venture capitalists can be the worst enemies of entrepreneurs.
zh: 所以他说，银行和风险资本家可能是企业家最坏的敌人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They create doubt in entrepreneurs' minds.
zh: 他们在企业家的头脑中制造怀疑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And worst of all, they think that an originator will be helped by their own, oh, this is funny.
zh: 最糟糕的是，他们认为一个原创者会从他们自己的——哦，这个很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And worst of all, they think that the originator, meaning him in this situation, will be helped by their oh so insightful views on how he or she should run the new business.
zh: 最糟糕的是，他们认为在这个情境下的创始者——也就是他本人——会因为他们对新业务应该如何经营的那些「极具洞察力」的看法而受益。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often, they kill off what's different, special, and full of potential.
zh: 他们常常扼杀那些独特的、特别的、充满潜力的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he gives an example of this happening early in his career, or early in the days of Bloomberg, I should say.
zh: 于是他举了一个例子，发生在他职业生涯早期，或者说应该说是彭博早期。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our early years, one venture capitalist came to see us.
zh: 在我们早年，有一位风险投资人来看我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: This guy was one of those self-entitled men who had been born on third base and thought he hit it triple.
zh: 这家伙属于那种自视甚高的男人，生在垒球三垒上却以为是自己打出的三垒安打。

speaker: Unknown
en: After telling us everything that we were doing was wrong,
zh: 在告诉我们我们所做的一切都是错的之后，

speaker: Unknown
en: and that we were too unstructured to survive and we were stupid because we were unable to predict future growth with specificity.
zh: 还说我们太没有章法、难以生存，还说我们很蠢，因为我们无法精确预测未来的增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: He left to advise his partners not to buy from Bloomberg.
zh: 他离开后建议他的合伙人不要购买彭博的服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason?
zh: 原因是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't show much interest in his views on how to run our company.
zh: 我们对他关于如何经营我们公司的看法没表现出多大兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was sure right about that account.
zh: 关于那个账户他倒说得完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Bloomberg, and then he's talking about work on product and sales first and work on them in parallel, and then you can work on everything else after that.
zh: 在彭博——然后他谈到先做产品和销售，并行推进它们，之后你再去处理其他所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Bloomberg, we always built the product first.
zh: 在彭博，我们总是先打造产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think about accounting and shipping much later in the process.
zh: 我们把会计和出货放在流程中更晚的阶段去考虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Selling is the only process we run simultaneously with development from the start.
zh: 销售是我们从一开始唯一与开发同时进行的流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he talks about the very humble first days of what becomes one of the most valuable private companies.
zh: 然后他谈到了这家日后成为最有价值的私人公司之一的企业的最初那段非常简朴的日子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ever created, I rented a one-room temporary office.
zh: 有史以来所创造的公司之一，我租了一间临时的一室办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was about 100 square feet of space with a view of an alley.
zh: 那是个大约100平方英尺的空间，能看到一条小巷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I deposited $300,000 of my Salomon Brothers Windfall into a corporate checking account.
zh: 我把所罗门兄弟给我的意外之财中的30万美元存进了一个公司支票账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And 15 years later, I had a billion-dollar business.
zh: 15年后，我有了一家价值10亿美元的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And before we get back into this, I want to tell you about AppLovin.
zh: 在我们继续之前，我想跟你讲讲 AppLovin。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my all-time favorite quotes is from the book Zero to One.
zh: 我最喜欢的名言之一来自《从0到1》这本书。

speaker: Unknown
en: In that book, Peter Thiel writes, he says, the single most powerful pattern I have noticed is that successful people find value in unexpected places, and they do this by thinking about business from first principles instead of formulas.
zh: 在那本书里，Peter Thiel 写道，他说，我注意到的最强大的单一模式是，成功的人在意想不到的地方发现价值，而他们做到这一点，是通过第一性原理而非公式来思考商业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is exactly what AppLovin has done with their advertising platform.
zh: 而这正是 AppLovin 用他们的广告平台所做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: AppLovin connects you with over a billion potential new customers in mobile games.
zh: AppLovin 让你与超过10亿潜在新客户在移动游戏中建立连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: AppLovin allows you to capture undivided attention.
zh: AppLovin 让你能够捕获完整的注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: AppLovin ads are full screen videos that are watched for an average of 35 seconds.
zh: AppLovin 的广告是全屏视频，平均观看时长为35秒。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is retention that blows other ad platforms out of the water.
zh: 这是把其他广告平台远远甩在身后的留存率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can launch on AppLovin in minutes.
zh: 而你可以在几分钟内在 AppLovin 上启动。

speaker: Unknown
en: You set the goal and AppLovin achieves it.
zh: 你设定目标，AppLovin 实现它。

speaker: Unknown
en: No complex setup, no expertise needed.
zh: 无需复杂设置，无需专业知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: And AppLovin scales quickly.
zh: 而且 AppLovin 扩展速度很快。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can put your ads in front of over a billion potential customers.
zh: 他们可以把你的广告展示在超过10亿潜在客户面前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other businesses have seen immediate results, scaled to hundreds of thousands of dollars of spend per day, and increased their revenue by millions.
zh: 其他企业已经看到了立竿见影的效果，规模扩大到每天数十万美元的投放，并增加了数百万美元的收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you want to get started quickly before all of your competitors are on AppLovin.
zh: 所以你要在所有竞争对手都上 AppLovin 之前尽快开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can do that by going to AppLovin.com.
zh: 你可以访问 AppLovin.com 来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's AppLovin.com.
zh: 那就是 AppLovin.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I want to tell you about Vanta.
zh: 然后我想跟你讲讲 Vanta。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vanta, Vanta, Vanta.
zh: Vanta、Vanta、Vanta。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vanta helps your company prove you're secure so more customers will use your product or service.
zh: Vanta 帮助你的公司证明你是安全的，从而让更多客户使用你的产品或服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vanta is an AI powered security expert that scales with you.
zh: Vanta 是一个随你一起扩展的 AI 驱动的安全专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: The more your business grows, the more complex your security needs get.
zh: 你的业务增长越多，你的安全需求就越复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that complexity turns into chaos.
zh: 而这种复杂会变成混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vanta tames that chaos for you.
zh: Vanta 为你驯服这种混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vanta automates compliance, continuously monitors your controls, and gives you a single source of truth for compliance and risk.
zh: Vanta 将合规自动化，持续监控你的控制措施，并为你提供合规与风险的单一可信来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: So whether you're a fast growing startup or an enterprise company,
zh: 所以无论你是一家快速成长的初创公司还是一家大型企业，

speaker: Unknown
en: Vanta fits easily into your existing workflows.
zh: Vanta 都能轻松融入你现有的工作流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many companies won't sign contracts unless you're certified, and this is causing you to lose out on sales.
zh: 许多公司除非你持有认证，否则不会签署合同，这正导致你失去销售机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is why the average Vanta customer reports a 526% return on investment after becoming a Vanta customer.
zh: 这就是为什么 Vanta 的平均客户报告在成为 Vanta 客户后获得526%的投资回报率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Automate your compliance, security, and trust with Vanta.
zh: 用 Vanta 将你的合规、安全和信任自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vanta will help you win trust, close deals, and stay secure faster and with less effort.
zh: Vanta 将帮你赢得信任、更快且更省力地达成交易并保持安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to vanta.com forward slash founders and you'll get $1,000 off.
zh: 访问 vanta.com 斜杠 founders,你将获得 1,000 美元的折扣。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is vanta.com forward slash founders.
zh: 网址是 vanta.com 斜杠 founders。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's going to take him some time to figure out what product to build and then to build that product.
zh: 所以他需要一些时间来搞清楚要做什么产品,然后把那个产品做出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in the meantime, he needs to bring in money.
zh: 在此期间,他需要弄到钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he has this idea.

speaker: Unknown
en: He's like, OK, try to do some kind of service related business.
zh: 他说,好吧,试着做某种服务类的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's see if we can do some consulting.
zh: 我们看看能不能做点咨询。

speaker: Unknown
en: This brings in, you know, a couple hundred thousand dollars.
zh: 这带来了,你知道,几十万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he writes, right after forming our company, we did some consulting.
zh: 于是他写道,公司刚成立后,我们做了一些咨询。

speaker: Unknown
en: It brought in cash, gave us exposure and helped provide us with some legitimacy that would later lead to work for more clients.
zh: 它带来了现金,给了我们曝光度,并帮助我们获得了一定的正当性,这些后来为我们带来了更多客户的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it bought us our first sale to Merrill Lynch.
zh: 它还为我们买下了第一笔销售,卖给了 Merrill Lynch。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I love that he sold to Merrill Lynch before he had a product.
zh: 我很喜欢他在还没有产品之前就把东西卖给了 Merrill Lynch。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I came back from the meeting, my colleagues were elated until the reality of a six-month delivery for something that didn't exist began to sink in.
zh: 当我开完会回来,我的同事们欣喜若狂,直到一个根本不存在的东西要六个月交付的现实开始被意识到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like, okay, we sell this product doesn't exist.
zh: 就是说,好吧,我们卖了这个产品,但产品不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we say, don't worry, it doesn't exist.
zh: 我们说,别担心,它虽然不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to have it six months from now.
zh: 但六个月后你们就会拿到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: He just made up the day.
zh: 他就是随口编了个日子。

speaker: Unknown
en: As developers, we're magicians, not miracle workers.
zh: 作为开发者,我们是魔术师,但不是创造奇迹的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Month after month as we worked, our mood alternated between elation and the feeling of an impending disaster.
zh: 月复一月地工作,我们的情绪在狂喜和灾难临头的感觉之间交替。

speaker: Unknown
en: We weren't just putting out fires, we were adjusting to major earthquakes when some new software bug forced us to start over.
zh: 我们不只是在一味救火,当某个新的软件漏洞迫使我们从头再来时,我们是在适应大地震。

speaker: Unknown
en: But every day we got closer to building the machine that we promised.
zh: 但每一天,我们都离造出我们承诺的那台机器更近一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the time, he's also building hardware.
zh: 那时候,他同时还在造硬件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which we'll talk about.
zh: 这个我们后面会聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's got a lot of great ideas about that, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一句,他在这方面有很多很棒的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Essentially, he looks at his business as just content, like data and analytics.
zh: 本质上,他把自己的业务看作只是内容,比如数据和分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he built hardware when he needed to build hardware, but once somebody came along that could build better hardware than him, he just focused on what his actual business was, and he never confused what his business was with the device that delivered it.
zh: 当他需要造硬件时他就造硬件,但一旦有人能造出比他更好的硬件,他就专注于自己真正的业务是什么,他从不把自己真正的业务和交付业务的设备混为一谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: He has some great lines on that, which we'll get to in a minute.
zh: 他对此有一些很妙的表述,我们一会儿会讲到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our style then was pretty much the same as today.
zh: 我们当时的风格和今天基本一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We took the problem and broke it down into little, manageable, digestible pieces.
zh: 我们把问题拆解成一个个小的、可管理的、易于消化的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then each of us took responsibility for the one we were best suited to do.
zh: 然后我们每个人承担自己最适合做的那一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he goes back to this idea, get action.
zh: 然后他又回到这个理念:行动起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: We acted from day one, others plan to plan for months.
zh: 我们从第一天就开始行动,而其他人计划着去计划,一计划就是好几个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: I must admit, I was worried.
zh: 我必须承认,我当时很担心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Remember, he started the company with 300,000 of his own money.
zh: 记住,他用自己 30 万美元创办了这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now he's 4 million into this thing.
zh: 现在他已经在这件事上投进去 400 万了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He only has 10 million to his name.
zh: 他名下只有 1,000 万。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were spending what would grow to be a $4 million investment of my $10 million.
zh: 我们花的钱,将成长为对我那 1,000 万中一笔 400 万的投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: Simultaneously, I was becoming responsible for families of almost two dozen company employees.
zh: 与此同时,我也开始要对近二十几名公司员工的家庭负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: I convinced these people to follow me, and if the venture had not succeeded, I would have failed them, their spouses and their children, as well as our prospective customers.
zh: 我说服这些人跟随我,如果这个创业没有成功,我就辜负了他们、他们的配偶和他们的孩子,也辜负了我们潜在的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yet, we plowed ahead.
zh: 然而,我们还是奋力向前。

speaker: Unknown
en: From the beginning, I was convinced we were doing something that nobody else could do, nor was anyone even trying.
zh: 从一开始我就确信,我们做的事情别人做不了,甚至没有别人在尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our product would be the first in the investment business where normal people without specialized training could sit down, hit a key, and get an answer to financial questions, some of which they didn't even know they should ask.
zh: 我们的产品将是投资行业里的第一个:没有受过专业训练的普通人可以坐下来,敲一个键,就得到财务问题的答案,其中有些问题他们甚至不知道自己应该问。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over time, the Bloomberg terminal evolved to allow users to run an ever wider array of functions developed by our more than 5,000 programmers and engineers.
zh: 随着时间推移,Bloomberg 终端不断演进,允许用户运行由我们 5,000 多名程序员和工程师开发的越来越广泛的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it all began with a simple premise, putting more information at people's fingertips, more quickly and more accurately than they could otherwise get it.
zh: 但这一切都始于一个简单的前提:让人们更快、更准确地获得信息,比他们通过其他方式能获得的更快、更准确。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is still the heart of our business.
zh: 这至今仍是我们业务的核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I absolutely love this part because this describes, again, the beginning of his business.
zh: 然后我绝对热爱这一部分,因为这又一次描述了他业务的起点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finally, the day arrived, almost.
zh: 终于,那一天到来了,差不多吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: The six-month promise ran out on a Saturday, so we could postpone delivery until Monday.
zh: 六个月的承诺在周六到期,所以我们可以把交付推迟到周一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we're at six months and two days.
zh: 所以现在是六个月零两天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Monday didn't necessarily mean Monday morning.
zh: 而周一不一定意味着周一早上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be Monday afternoon.
zh: 也可能是周一下午。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were constantly having to fix the software, rewriting it again and again to deliver the consistency needed for reliable real-time analysis.
zh: 我们不得不不断地修软件，一遍又一遍地重写，以提供可靠实时分析所需的一致性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're out of control, I would shout, as each software bug surfaced.
zh: 每当一个软件 bug 冒出来，我就会大喊：我们失控了！

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to be out of business if this continues.
zh: 再这样下去我们就要关门了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I still say the same things today.
zh: 今天我仍然说着同样的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was June 1983, and we had delivered something on time, close to, something that worked, sort of, and a machine that would be useful, somewhat.
zh: 那是 1983 年 6 月，我们按时交付了——差不多按时——一个能用的东西，勉强能用，还有一台多少会有用的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we get to the very important role that Merrill Lynch plays in Bloomberg Stories, not only their first customer, they're their first major investor.
zh: 那太令人满足了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in 1982, this is going to blow your mind, 1982 they buy...
zh: 所以在 1982 年，这会让你大吃一惊，1982 年他们买下了……

speaker: Unknown
en: 30% of the company for $30 million, okay?
zh: 用 3000 万美元买下公司 30% 的股份，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's in 1982.
zh: 那是在 1982 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And around 1996, Michael Bloomberg buys back 10% of the 30%, okay?
zh: 大约在 1996 年，Michael Bloomberg 买回了那 30% 中的 10%,好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: 10% for $200 million.
zh: 10% 花了 2 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then about 10 years later in 2008, Michael Bloomberg buys the remaining 20% that Merrill Lynch still owned from this investment they made in 1982 for $4.4 billion.
zh: 然后大约 10 年后，在 2008 年，Michael Bloomberg 以 44 亿美元买下了 Merrill Lynch 从 1982 年那笔投资中仍持有的剩余 20%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a way to think about that is for $30 million invested in 1982, Merrill Lynch makes what?
zh: 所以一个理解方式是：Merrill Lynch 在 1982 年投资了 3000 万美元，赚了多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: About $4.6 billion.
zh: 大约 46 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not only that, they helped him understand the product he was building.
zh: 不仅如此，他们还帮他理解了他正在打造的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he has two traders working at Merrill Lynch that are essentially telling him everything about the product that needs to be fixed so it's useful to them.
zh: 他有两个在 Merrill Lynch 工作的交易员，基本上在告诉他关于这个产品需要修复的一切，好让它对他们有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And therefore, it's useful to them.
zh: 因此，它对他们就有用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be useful to the future tens of thousands, maybe hundreds of thousands of people just like them.
zh: 它也可能对将来成千上万——也许几十万——和他们一样的人有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we first installed it, Merrill assigned two traders to work with us.
zh: 我们第一次安装它时，Merrill 派了两名交易员来和我们一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought they'd be real pains and second-guess us every step of the way.
zh: 我本以为他们会非常难缠，事事都质疑我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was I wrong?
zh: 我错得有多离谱？

speaker: Unknown
en: It turned out both of them were as responsible for success as anyone.
zh: 结果他们两个人和其他任何人一样，对成功负有责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were nitpickers, but not in a nasty way.
zh: 他们是爱挑刺的人，但不是恶意的挑刺。

speaker: Unknown
en: They wanted us to succeed.
zh: 他们希望我们成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: When they said something didn't work, they could show us it didn't work, so we knew for sure it didn't work, and more important, to help fix the problem under what specific circumstances it didn't work.
zh: 当他们说某个东西不好用时，他们能演示给我们看它确实不好用，所以我们确信它不好用，更重要的是，帮我们弄清在什么具体情况下它不好用，从而修复问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every day, our system got better as we fixed each problem they pointed out.
zh: 每天，随着我们修好他们指出的每一个问题，我们的系统都在变好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd always rather have a smart, fair, honest, demanding client than a nasty dummy or an I don't care user.
zh: 我总是宁愿要一个聪明、公正、诚实、要求高的客户，也不要一个恶劣的蠢货或一个无所谓的用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then more about the early days, which I think were his favorite part of the company, the fact that you should be doing everything yourselves at the beginning.
zh: 再多讲讲早期日子，我觉得那是他最喜欢的公司阶段：一开始你应该事事亲力亲为。

speaker: Unknown
en: For our first three or four years in business, I did all of these functions.
zh: 在我们做生意的头三四年里，所有这些职能都是我一个人做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked full-time selling our services, negotiating all of our supplier and customer contracts, and running the company.
zh: 我全职做销售服务，谈我们所有的供应商和客户合同，并且管理公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Never before or since did I have as much fun and as challenging a time in business.
zh: 在那之前或之后，我在生意中再也没有过那么快乐、那么有挑战的时光。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back when we started, the original half dozen of us, after finishing our regular jobs, would go into clients' offices on the weekends.
zh: 在我们刚起步的时候，最初那六个人，做完本职工作后，周末会去客户的办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would crawl under the new customers' desks and we'd lay our own cables.
zh: 我们会爬到新客户桌子底下，自己铺线缆。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would drag wires, stuffing the cables through holes that we drilled in other people's furnitures, all without permission, without giving any thought to any fire law or building code.
zh: 我们会拖电线，把线缆塞过我们在别人家具上钻的洞里，全都没经过许可，完全没考虑任何消防法规或建筑规范。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's amazing we didn't burn down some office or electrocute ourselves.
zh: 我们没烧掉哪个办公室、也没把自己电死，真是奇迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end of the day, 10 or 11 o'clock at night, we'd turn it on and watch what we created come alive.
zh: 到了一天结束，晚上十点或十一点，我们会把它打开，看着我们创造的东西活过来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was so satisfying.
zh: 真是太让人满足了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We improvised everything as we went along.
zh: 我们一路走一路即兴发挥。

speaker: Unknown
en: I gotta stop there.
zh: 我得在这里停一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's used the word improvise, steering the boat, you know, a little bit every day, just to use the words of Henry Singleton.
zh: 他用过「即兴发挥」这个词，每天稍微调一调船的方向，借用 Henry Singleton 的话说。

speaker: Unknown
en: He uses that over and over again.
zh: 他一遍又一遍地使用这个说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We improvised every day.
zh: 我们每天都在即兴发挥。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just came and we iterated and got better every day.
zh: 我们就是来了，然后迭代，每天变好。

speaker: Unknown
en: The difference is...
zh: 区别在于……

speaker: Unknown
en: He iterated, got better every day, and didn't stop for 50 years.
zh: 他迭代，每天变好，而且 50 年没有停下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to write all the checks myself.
zh: 过去所有的支票都是我自己写的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I signed every contract.
zh: 每一份合同都是我签的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I paid every bill.
zh: 每一张账单都是我付的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did the hiring and firing.
zh: 我负责招聘和解雇。

speaker: Unknown
en: I bought the coffee, soda, cookies, and chips.
zh: 我买咖啡、汽水、饼干和薯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: I emptied the waste paper baskets.
zh: 我倒废纸篓。

speaker: Unknown
en: I dusted the windowsills.
zh: 我擦窗台上的灰。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wrote and handed out the paychecks personally.
zh: 我亲手写工资支票并亲自发放。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those were the best days.
zh: 那是最好的日子。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first few years in the early 1980s, we were involved in every aspect of our company.
zh: 在 1980 年代初的头几年,我们参与了公司的每一个方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: As we grew and turned these functions over to newly hired specialists, I felt like I was losing a child to adolescence.
zh: 随着我们壮大,把这些职能移交给新招聘的专家时,我感觉自己像失去了一个进入青春期的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good for the kid, but painful for the parent.
zh: 对孩子是好事,但对父母来说是痛苦的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we get to one of my favorite parts of the book, and this is where he starts building out the media part of his company.
zh: 然后我们来到这本书中我最喜欢的部分之一,这就是他开始打造公司媒体业务的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Starts with this guy named Matt Winkler, who's a reporter at the Wall Street Journal.
zh: 从一个叫 Matt Winkler 的人说起,他是《华尔街日报》的记者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keeps hearing about Bloomberg and this Bloomberg terminal and trying to figure out, okay, what's going on?
zh: 他不断听到关于 Bloomberg 和这个 Bloomberg 终端的消息,试图搞明白:好吧,这是怎么回事?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like he's hearing about it throughout the finance industry.
zh: 他在整个金融行业里都听到关于它的消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, okay, I'm going to go and like interview Michael Bloomberg.
zh: 然后他想:好吧,我要去采访 Michael Bloomberg。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in this part of the book, this is where Bloomberg is describing this first meeting they have.
zh: 于是在书的这一部分,Bloomberg 描述了他们的第一次会面。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, when they arrived in my office, I offered them the same speech that I used to convince people to take jobs with us.
zh: 他说,当他们走进我的办公室时,我向他们讲了我常用来说服人们加入我们公司的那套说辞。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got the best people in the world working here.
zh: 我们这里有世界上最优秀的人在这里工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of them think they walk on water.
zh: 他们每个人都觉得自己能在水面上行走。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of them are workaholics.
zh: 而这确实是个好主意,不管你是在跟一个记者谈话,还是在试图招募某个人加入你的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once they come, they stay for the rest of their lives because they love it.
zh: 一旦来了,他们就会待上一辈子,因为他们热爱这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've built the better mousetrap.
zh: 他们造出了更好的捕鼠器。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're doing something important.
zh: 他们在做重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're giving the little guy information he needs to fight.
zh: 他们把小人物抗争所需的信息交到他们手上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's saying, you know,
zh: 他说,你知道,

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing for him to say that he's got the, you know, the best product, the best people, but he said, you don't have to believe me.
zh: 他说自己拥有最好的产品、最好的人,这是一回事,但他说,你不必相信我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here, he does something really smart.
zh: 在这里,他做了一件非常聪明的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he actually, it's a good idea whether you're talking to, I guess, a reporter or even trying to recruit somebody to join your company.
zh: 他其实——这是个好主意,不管你是在跟记者交谈,还是在试图招募某个人加入你的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he comes into, leaves the room, comes back with this big, thick printout.
zh: 他离开房间,回来时拿着一大厚沓打印件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he goes, here's every customer we have by name, by firm, and by phone number.
zh: 他说,这是我们的每一个客户,按姓名、公司和电话号码排列。

speaker: Unknown
en: Call them yourself.
zh: 你自己打给他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And essentially verify everything I just told you is true.
zh: 基本上就是去核实我刚才告诉你的一切是否属实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as Michael Bloomberg builds a relationship with Matt Winkler, he starts seeking Matt's advice.
zh: 于是在 Michael Bloomberg 与 Matt Winkler 建立关系的过程中,他开始寻求 Matt 的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really the main point of this section I think is really important.
zh: 这一节真正的要点我认为非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, hey, your company likely has information that no one else has.
zh: 就是:嘿,你的公司很可能拥有别人没有的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Start thinking about how you can repurpose it to benefit other people and then achieve your objective.
zh: 开始思考如何把它重新利用起来去造福他人,然后实现你的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's on the phone with Matt and he goes, hey, I want to make our terminal indispensable to stock as well as bond traders.
zh: 于是他在电话里对 Matt 说:嘿,我想让我们的终端对股票和债券交易员都不可或缺。

speaker: Unknown
en: Should we get into the text news business?
zh: 我们应该进入文字新闻业务吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: His answer wasn't what I expected, although it encouraged me to keep the conversation going.
zh: 他的回答出乎我的意料,尽管这鼓励我继续这场对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike, he said, you and the people who work with you have created a terminal that explains more about why bonds fluctuate each minute, each day, and each week than any collection of reporters ever could.
zh: Mike,他说,你和与你共事的人创造了一个终端,它对债券为何每分钟、每天、每周波动的解释,比任何一群记者所能做到的都要多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You already provide charts and graphs.
zh: 你们已经在提供图表和图形。

speaker: Unknown
en: That influenced the major debt trading decisions worldwide.
zh: 那些影响着全世界主要的债券交易决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Add text to that information and you'll have something that doesn't exist anywhere else.
zh: 在这些信息上加上文字,你就会拥有一个其他任何地方都不存在的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one in debt or equity will be able to live without it."
zh: 债券和股票领域没有人能离得开它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we see he goes back to this habit that he has.
zh: 然后我们看到他又回到了他的一个习惯。

speaker: Unknown
en: He consults history when trying to decide if he should enter the news business, right?
zh: 他在决定是否应该进入新闻业务时,会参考历史,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So he says, history shows that any gutsy entrepreneur, Joseph Pulitzer, William Randolph Hearst, Henry Luce,
zh: 所以他说,历史表明,任何有胆识的企业家——Joseph Pulitzer、William Randolph Hearst、Henry Luce、

speaker: Unknown
en: BC Forbes, Ted Turner, Rupert Murdoch, and Oprah Winfrey can enter the news business any time.
zh: BC Forbes、Ted Turner、Rupert Murdoch 和 Oprah Winfrey——随时都可以进入新闻行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he compares his advantage that he has that these other historical figures did not.
zh: 然后他比较了自己拥有的、这些历史人物所没有的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: Best of all, we had revenue from terminal rentals, which meant we didn't have to worry about a news service paying for itself as a standalone product.
zh: 最棒的是,我们有终端租赁的收入,这意味着我们不必担心新闻服务作为一种独立产品能否自负盈亏。

speaker: Unknown
en: One heck of an advantage.
zh: 这是一个了不起的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fundamentally, at Bloomberg, we're builders, not buyers.
zh: 从根本上说，在 Bloomberg,我们是建造者，不是买家。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it has never occurred to me to acquire a news organization as a starting point.
zh: 所以我从未想过把收购一家新闻机构作为起点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's always more fun to create from scratch and a lot less risky.
zh: 从零开始创造总是更有趣，而且风险小得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is the initial idea of this media business that he begins to build.
zh: 于是这就是他开始着手打造的这个媒体业务的最初构想。

speaker: Unknown
en: I handed him a three page list of what Bloomberg News should be doing.
zh: 我递给他一份三页的清单，写明 Bloomberg News 应该做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our purpose was to do more than just collect and relay news.
zh: 我们的目的不只是收集和转发新闻。

speaker: Unknown
en: It should also advertise the analytical and computational powers of the Bloomberg terminal.
zh: 它还应该宣传 Bloomberg 终端的分析和计算能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: By highlighting its capabilities in each news story.
zh: 方法就是在每一条新闻中突出它的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: With our terminal functions included, each of our news stories would be more informative than the competitors and more people would want to access them.
zh: 由于包含了我们的终端功能，我们的每一条新闻都会比竞争对手的信息更丰富，就会有更多人想要获取它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: This meant more revenue, which in turn meant we could afford more reporters and have more news and so on.
zh: 这意味着更多收入，而收入增加又意味着我们雇得起更多记者、有更多新闻，如此循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: So think about it.
zh: 想想看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each news story is a product demo.
zh: 每一条新闻就是一个产品演示。

speaker: Unknown
en: More demos lead to more revenue.
zh: 更多演示带来更多收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: More revenue leads to more stories and even more revenue.
zh: 更多收入带来更多报道，乃至更多收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is the part I mentioned earlier about really understanding what the actual business that you're in.
zh: 这就是我之前提到的那一点：真正理解你身处的是一个什么样的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we first began, we manufactured computers and keyboards because we had to.
zh: 我们起步时，我们制造计算机和键盘，因为不得不这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Personal computers didn't really exist in order to deliver our product.
zh: 当时个人计算机基本还不存在，没法用来交付我们的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we never made the mistake of believing that we were in the hardware business.
zh: 但我们从未犯过那种错误，以为自己身处硬件行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are in the business of producing and distributing the world's most accurate, reliable, comprehensive, up to the second information and analysis.
zh: 我们这行是生产和分发世界上最准确、最可靠、最全面、最实时的信息与分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has been our mission from day one, and it has never changed.
zh: 这从第一天起就是我们的使命，从未改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Technology will continuously revolutionize distribution, but our product is content.
zh: 技术会不断革新分发方式，但我们的产品是内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: It remains consistent.
zh: 它始终如一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Much of that content sits behind the media world's most expensive paywall.
zh: 其中大部分内容都藏在媒体界最昂贵的付费墙后面。

speaker: Unknown
en: A subscription to Bloomberg costs about $22,000 a year.
zh: 一份 Bloomberg 的订阅每年大约 22,000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's almost 20 years old.
zh: 我想它差不多有 20 年历史了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the price is over 30,000 a year, if I'm not mistaken.
zh: 如果我没记错的话，现在价格每年超过 30,000。

speaker: Unknown
en: That works out to be about $88 per workday.
zh: 折算下来大约每个工作日 88 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: When customers complain that it's expensive, we tell them, if you can't make $88 a day using Bloomberg, you have a bigger problem than our bill.
zh: 当客户抱怨它贵时，我们会告诉他们：如果你用 Bloomberg 一天都赚不回 88 美元，那你面对的问题就比我们的账单更大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he's got some great advice on how to make your product or your company stand out.
zh: 接着他给了一些很好的建议，教你如何让你的产品或公司脱颖而出。

speaker: Unknown
en: I should say, at this point in the story, his company is not called Bloomberg.
zh: 说到这里我该说明一下，他的公司当时还不叫 Bloomberg。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's called Innovative Market Systems.
zh: 它叫 Innovative Market Systems。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's about to change that.
zh: 而他即将改变这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he says, entrepreneurs in the booming 1980s were commonplace.
zh: 他是这么说的：在繁荣的 1980 年代，企业家随处可见。

speaker: Unknown
en: My company was small and virtually anonymous.
zh: 我的公司规模很小，几乎默默无闻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our product, the market data terminal that we were selling, was called MarketMaster.
zh: 我们的产品，也就是我们销售的行情数据终端，叫 MarketMaster。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it could have been confused with a kitchen appliance.
zh: 它很容易被误认为是一件厨房电器。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one knew us.
zh: 没人知道我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one cared about me.
zh: 没人在意我。

speaker: Unknown
en: But by 1984, this was about to change.
zh: 但到 1984 年，这一切即将改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those were the days when Ronald Reagan proved how marketable ideas could be when they were peddled with charisma.
zh: 那是 Ronald Reagan 证明了当理念被以个人魅力兜售时可以多么畅销的年代。

speaker: Unknown
en: You needed a spokesperson for mass appeal.
zh: 你需要一个能吸引大众的代言人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Consumers and the media identified products and policies with the people who pitched them.
zh: 消费者和媒体把产品与政策同推销它们的人画上等号。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's actually a very old idea.
zh: 这其实是一个非常古老的理念。

speaker: Unknown
en: You and I have talked about David Ogilvie, Albert Lasker, Claude Hopkins.
zh: 你和我聊过 David Ogilvie、Albert Lasker、Claude Hopkins。

speaker: Unknown
en: In any case, they tried to get away from the company and basically have like a spokesperson, even if it wasn't the founder.
zh: 无论如何，他们试图跳出公司本身，基本上就是找一个代言人，即便那个人不是创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they wanted, they said, people identify with people, not products and not companies.
zh: 但他们想要的是，他们说，人们认同的是人，不是产品，也不是公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And essentially, we're what?
zh: 而本质上，我们现在是多久以后？

speaker: Unknown
en: 60 years later, then Albert Lasker and Claude Hopkins were applying that same exact idea to all kinds of different products.
zh: 60 年后，而当年 Albert Lasker 和 Claude Hopkins 正是把完全相同的理念应用于各种不同的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: He just happens to apply it to his own product.
zh: 他只不过恰好把这个理念用在了自己的产品上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need a spokesperson for mass appeal.
zh: 所以你需要一个能吸引大众的代言人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Consumers in the media identify products and policies with people who pitch them.
zh: 媒体消费者会把产品和政策与推销它们的人联系起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nike didn't just make sneakers.
zh: Nike 不只是做运动鞋。

speaker: Unknown
en: It pushed them with the mystique that could only come from Michael Jordan.
zh: 它借助唯有 Michael Jordan 才能带来的神秘感来推广它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: To have the best mousetrap wasn't enough.
zh: 仅有最好的捕鼠器是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Success was delivered by people promotion.
zh: 成功是靠人的推广实现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we were going to build our business, we too needed a personality.
zh: 如果我们要建立自己的企业，我们也需要一个有个性的人物。

speaker: Unknown
en: The obvious choice?
zh: 显而易见的人选？

speaker: Unknown
en: Me.
zh: 我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our competitors' founders were all dead.
zh: 我们竞争对手的创始人都已经去世了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I, on the other hand, were alive and out making speeches and sales calls every day in city after city around the world, turning my name and work into a great weapon that others in the financial news and market data businesses could not match.
zh: 而我呢，还活着，每天都在一个又一个城市、在世界各地发表演讲、打销售电话，把我的名字和工作变成金融新闻和市场数据行业中其他人无法匹敌的强大武器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And since I'd spent so much time demonstrating our product, people had begun to mentally interchange me with the terminal.
zh: 而且因为我花了那么多时间演示我们的产品，人们在心里已经开始把我与终端混为一谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before they were called Bloomberg Terminals.
zh: 在它们被称为 Bloomberg 终端之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'd say, hey, give me, instead of saying, what was his name, Market Master, which is a terrible name, by the way, or even they're using the word terminal, they're just like, hey, give me some of these Bloombergs.
zh: 他们会说，嘿，给我来一台，而不是说那个他叫什么名字来着，Market Master——顺便说一句，这名字起得很糟糕——或者甚至他们在用“终端”这个词，他们就是会说，嘿，给我来几台这些 Bloombergs。

speaker: Unknown
en: I acquiesced to a decision that the marketplace already had made.
zh: 我默许了市场已经做出的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Henceforth, the product and the company itself would be Bloomberg.
zh: 从此以后，产品和公司本身都叫 Bloomberg。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he has a hilarious line here.
zh: 然后他这里有一句非常搞笑的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would become the Colonel Sanders of Financial Information Services.
zh: 我将成为金融信息服务领域的 Colonel Sanders。

speaker: Unknown
en: As the owner, by definition, I spoke with authority.
zh: 作为所有者，理所当然地，我说话是有权威的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to make good copy, I gave the press a colorful personality to focus on.
zh: 而且为了制造好素材，我给了媒体一个 colourful 的个性来聚焦。

speaker: Unknown
en: You kind of see, obviously, I think if you're listening to this, you probably already know, you've heard his name, you know about his business, but you can see he's, you know, he likes the, he has a colorful personality.
zh: 你多少能看出来，显然，我想如果你在听这个节目，你大概已经知道了，你听过他的名字，你知道他的生意，但你能看出他，你知道的，他喜欢那种，他有一个很 colorful 的个性。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's unapologetically extreme.
zh: 他毫不掩饰地极端。

speaker: Unknown
en: He talks a lot of shit throughout this book.
zh: 他在这本书里说了很多大话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He has a perspective, a point of view, and he used that perspective, that personality, that point of view to build his company.
zh: 他有自己的视角、自己的观点，而他正是用那种视角、那种个性、那种观点建立了他的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then he talks about this very important extension for his media business where he expands into television and radio.
zh: 然后他谈到了对他的媒体业务非常重要的一个扩展，他扩张到了电视和广播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the interesting part about this, and it goes against his idea that he doesn't want to buy things, he wants to build them.
zh: 而这有趣的地方在于，这与他不想买东西、而是想自己建造的理念相悖。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one, he didn't want to do television and radio.
zh: 所以第一，他本来不想做电视和广播。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the person had asked him three times.
zh: 我记得那个人问了他三次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then two, he realizes, oh, it's actually smarter in this case.
zh: 然后第二，他意识到，哦，在这个情况下其实更聪明的做法是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can buy something that I kind of jumpstart this process.
zh: 我可以买下某个东西，以此跳过启动这个流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, it goes back to this flexibility that, you know, he has this goal, this end goal.
zh: 再一次，这又回到了那种灵活性，你知道的，他有一个目标，一个最终目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: He has a basic idea of where he's going to go, but he doesn't know how he's going to get there and he's willing to be flexible every day.
zh: 他对自己要往哪里去有一个基本的想法，但他不知道他会怎么到达那里，而且他愿意每天都保持灵活。

speaker: Unknown
en: This guy named John Fram calls him.
zh: 有个叫 John Fram 的人给他打电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: John was an employee at the FNN.
zh: John 是 FNN 的一名员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: The FNN was the Financial News Network.
zh: FNN 是 Financial News Network(金融新闻网)。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a television channel whose parent was in bankruptcy.
zh: 它是一个电视频道，其母公司正处于破产状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: He told me I should buy FNN.
zh: 他告诉我我应该买下 FNN。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike, what you really need to do is get into television.
zh: Mike，你真正需要做的是进军电视。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will create synergies with everything else you're doing.
zh: 它会为你正在做的一切创造协同效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: What a dumb idea, I said, cutting them off.
zh: 多愚蠢的主意啊，我说，打断了他。

speaker: Unknown
en: My operating principle has always been build, don't buy.
zh: 我的经营原则一直是自己建造，而不是购买。

speaker: Unknown
en: Besides, what did I have to do with television?
zh: 再说了，我和电视能有什么关系？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the price of this television network at the time was $200 million.
zh: 我记得这个电视网络当时的价格是两亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's like, listen, I'm not spending $200 million on this, no matter what you say, you're crazy.
zh: 他就像，听着，不管你怎么说我都不会在这上面花两亿美元，你疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Guy calls him back the next day, starts talking to him as if we're old friends.
zh: 那家伙第二天又打来电话，开始跟他聊得就像我们是老朋友一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: He suggested now instead of he goes, so you should buy this, but then you also need somebody in-house to develop audio and video programming at Bloomberg and you should hire me and two other guys to do this.
zh: 他建议说，不再是他说的那种“所以你应该买下这个”，而是你还需要一个内部的人来开发 Bloomberg 的音频和视频节目，你应该雇用我和另外两个人来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once again, I said television and radio makes no sense for Bloomberg and I hung up the phone.
zh: 我再一次说，电视和广播对 Bloomberg 毫无意义，然后我挂了电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: A few days passed and then I got another call from him.
zh: 几天过去了，然后我又接到了他的一个电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I listened to a longer version of the pitch he made a few days earlier, it occurred to me, one of us is stupid and it isn't him.
zh: 当我听着他几天前那个推销词的更长版本时，我突然意识到，我们两个当中有一个是蠢货，而那个人不是他。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I hired the three of them that day.
zh: 所以我当天就雇用了他们三个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the first thing they do is,
zh: 于是他们做的第一件事是，

speaker: Unknown
en: They start going out and buying radio stations.
zh: 他们开始出去收购电台。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then from radio, they start pushing and extending into television.
zh: 然后从电台开始，他们开始向电视领域推进和扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he talks about this.
zh: 他谈到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, this is, I think, one of the most important parts of the book.
zh: 再说一次，我认为这是这本书最重要的部分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's got like a lot of these like roundabout ways to get in front of potential customers.
zh: 他有很多这种迂回的方式来接触到潜在客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is maybe one of the most genius things he's ever done is obviously the media component of his business.
zh: 我想这可能是他有史以来做得最天才的事情之一，显然就是他业务中的媒体部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, people often ask me why Bloomberg ventured into radio and TV.
zh: 所以广播是我们在其他地方所做事情的轻松延伸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was there some hidden motive?
zh: 是不是有什么隐藏的动机？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the motive wasn't hidden.
zh: 而这个动机并不隐藏。

speaker: Unknown
en: The motive was to sell more subscriptions.
zh: 动机就是卖出更多订阅。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what his entire business runs on.
zh: 他的整个业务就是靠这个运转的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he talks about why he has an advantage of doing this.
zh: 他谈到了为什么他在这方面有优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, we have the necessary information and the technical know-how.
zh: 他说，我们拥有必要的信息和技术诀窍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So broadcasting is an easy extension of what we're doing elsewhere.
zh: 所以广播(roadcasting)是我们在其他地方所做的事情的一个简单延伸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Radio and television provide our company with instant visibility.
zh: 电台和电视为公司提供了即时的曝光度。

speaker: Unknown
en: The media like nothing better than writing about themselves.
zh: 媒体最喜欢莫过于写关于自己的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The more exposure Bloomberg has to the fourth estate, the more they'll promote us to the general public.
zh: Bloomberg 在第四等级(新闻界)面前曝光越多，他们就越会把我们推广给大众。

speaker: Unknown
en: To reach potential customers who don't yet subscribe to our print products, radio and TV help us get our message out.
zh: 为了触达那些还没订阅我们印刷产品的潜在客户，电台和电视帮助我们把我们的话语传出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: The people who lease our terminals are part of radio and television's masses.
zh: 租用我们终端的人也是电台和电视的大众受众的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: They need news while jogging, showering, driving, or sitting at home.
zh: 他们在慢跑、洗澡、开车或坐在家里时需要新闻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've got to give them what they need where they are.
zh: 而我们必须在他们所在的地方给他们所需的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Radio and television simply became another delivery mechanism for the same content.
zh: 电台和电视只是成为了同样内容的另一种传送机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every piece of content he produces...
zh: 而他制作的每一 piece 内容……

speaker: Unknown
en: is a ad for the Bloomberg subscription.
zh: 都是 Bloomberg 订阅的广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he talks about the same idea a few pages later.
zh: 几页之后他又谈到同样的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, everything they do increases the likelihood of selling Bloomberg subscriptions.
zh: 再说一次，他们做的一切都在提高卖出 Bloomberg 订阅的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: TV stories relate to magazine articles that relate to the computer data.
zh: 电视报道与杂志文章相关，杂志文章又与计算机数据相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then he's got a great idea on how to pick the person that should lead the project, any new project inside your organization.
zh: 然后他有一个很棒的想法，关于如何挑选应该领导项目的人，即你组织内部的任何新项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a true capitalist, I've always believed in the market's ability to make efficient selections.
zh: 作为一个真正的资本家，我一直相信市场做出高效选择的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: In many of our new ventures, we do not appoint a manager at the beginning.
zh: 在我们的许多新业务中，我们在一开始并不任命经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: We simply throw everyone interested into the deep end of the pool, as it were, and stand back.
zh: 我们只是把所有感兴趣的人扔进泳池的深水区，可以这么说，然后退后观察。

speaker: Unknown
en: It becomes obvious very quickly who the best swimmers are.
zh: 谁是最好的游泳者很快就会变得显而易见。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just watch who people go to for help and advice, and later, when we formalize a management appointment, no one's ever surprised.
zh: 我们只观察人们会去找谁寻求帮助和建议，之后，当我们正式任命管理层时，没有人会感到意外。

speaker: Unknown
en: The leverage we gain from employing creative people and letting them do their own thing is incredible.
zh: 我们从雇用有创造力的人并让他们做自己的事情中获得的杠杆是不可思议的。

speaker: Unknown
en: A few pages later goes back again to that idea.
zh: 几页之后他又回到那个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything we're doing is just increasing the likelihood of selling more Bloomberg subscriptions.
zh: 我们做的一切都只是在提高卖出更多 Bloomberg 订阅的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our business is information, not the medium that the information is delivered into.
zh: 我们的业务是信息，而不是信息所交付的媒介。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see he's already been flexible about this multiple times.
zh: 你可以看到他已经多次在这方面表现出灵活性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why use all forms of media rather than focus on just one?
zh: 为什么要使用所有形式的媒体，而不是只专注于一种？

speaker: Unknown
en: What business are we in?
zh: 我们身处什么行业？

speaker: Unknown
en: Some companies declare themselves to be in radio or in television or newspapers and so on.
zh: 有些公司宣称自己身处电台行业、电视行业或报业等等。
