speaker: Unknown
en: We have a greater vision.
zh: 我们有更宏大的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bloomberg is in the business of giving its customers the information they need in whatever form is most appropriate.
zh: Bloomberg 的业务是以最合适的形式向客户提供他们需要的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: With all methods at our disposal, we do better.
zh: 有了所有可用的方法，我们做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We create or adopt a new medium.
zh: 我们创造或采用新的媒介。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do not ask our customers to accept less.
zh: 我们不要求我们的客户接受更少的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think this paragraph is interesting because he talks about the necessity for having a lot of self-confidence, having a big ego, but making sure your ego is not too big.
zh: 然后我认为这一段很有意思，因为他谈到有必要拥有大量的自信、拥有强大的自我，但要确保你的自我不要太大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he talked about, you know, the fact is he was a micromanager.
zh: 所以他谈到，你知道，事实是他是一个微管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had a really hard time delegating.
zh: 他非常难以授权。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he says, I was there in the beginning, and I too think I could do everything better than anyone else.
zh: 所以他说，我从一开始就在那里，我也认为我能把每件事做得比任何人都好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe in my design instincts and my sales savvy and my management skills are the best around.
zh: 我相信我的设计直觉、我的销售头脑和我的管理技能是身边最棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Still, my ego does allow for the remote possibility that someone might be as good at one or two little things.
zh: 尽管如此，我的自负还是容许了一种极小的可能性，即也许有人在某一件或两件小事上能和我一样好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've admitted there's a slim chance that ideas coming from others could be valuable as well.
zh: 我也承认，来自别人的想法有很小的概率也可能是有价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, I'm the same as every other entrepreneur, but at least I know what I don't know.
zh: 换句话说，我和所有其他创业者一样，但至少我知道自己不知道什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it goes back to this aggressive personality that he has, the fact that he's unapologetically extreme.
zh: 然后这又回到他所拥有的那种攻击性人格，即他毫不掩饰地极端。

speaker: Unknown
en: He considers his competitors as if they're trying to starve his children.
zh: 他把竞争对手看作是想饿死他孩子的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every day at Bloomberg, we face challenges that jeopardize our comfortable life.
zh: 在 Bloomberg 的每一天，我们都面临威胁我们舒适生活的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: We constantly have to fight established competitors trying to take food out of our children's mouths.
zh: 我们必须不断地与那些想从我们孩子嘴里夺走食物的老牌竞争对手斗争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there are the startups that want to destroy everything that we've built.
zh: 然后还有那些想摧毁我们已建成的一切的初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another thing that he repeats he has in common with Edmund Landon and Peter Thiel, this idea that you should not be making MeToo products.
zh: 他反复提到自己与 Edmund Landon 和 Peter Thiel 的另一个共同点，即你不应该做 MeToo 产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Edmund Landon says, don't waste your talents on MeToo products.
zh: Edmund Landon 说，不要把你的才华浪费在 MeToo 产品上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Peter Thiel says, don't build an undifferentiated commodity business.
zh: Peter Thiel 说，不要建立一个无差异化的同质化生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Michael Bloomberg says, what can we do that our competitors can't?
zh: Michael Bloomberg 说，我们能做什么是竞争对手做不到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no reason to do a copycat product.
zh: 没有理由去做一个山寨产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Consumers can just as easily buy from others.
zh: 消费者同样可以轻易地从别人那里购买。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he goes back to what he was saying at the beginning of the book, that he prefers a lot of these small bets with limited downside and uncapped upside.
zh: 然后他回到了他在书的开头所说的话，即他更喜欢那些下行有限、上行不封顶的小赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our modus operandi remains building from within, which avoids the bet-the-store, high-risk gambles that often characterize large takeovers, such as the disastrous Time Warner AOL deal.
zh: 我们的行事方式仍然是从内部构建，这避免了那种孤注一掷、高风险的赌博，而这类赌博往往是大额并购的特征，比如灾难性的 Time Warner AOL 交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I'm just not that smart.
zh: 也许我只是没那么聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I'm looking to expand, I prefer starting with a little capital that we can afford to lose and a few people we can always reassign to other projects.
zh: 当我寻求扩张时，我更喜欢从少量我们损失得起的资本和几个我们总能重新分配到其他项目的人开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: This way, we never feel we've committed to stay with our mistakes.
zh: 这样，我们永远不会觉得自己已经承诺要坚守我们的错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nor are we so overextended we can't handle other additional experimental ventures simultaneously.
zh: 我们也不会扩张过度，以至于无法同时处理其他额外的实验性业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then there's some hints in the book of just this unreal financial performance.
zh: 书里还有一些关于这种不真实的财务表现的暗示。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, I think he was like 98 or he might own 100% of the business now or like something like 98%.
zh: 再说一次，我记得他大概持有 98%,或者他现在可能拥有这家公司 100% 的股份，或者差不多 98%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he was like wildly successful almost from the beginning.
zh: 而且几乎从一开始他就极其成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a few years after founding Bloomberg, I think it was in the 90s.
zh: 所以在创立 Bloomberg 几年后，我记得是在 90 年代。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was making so much money in cash, he was giving away $200 million a year at charity.
zh: 他赚的现金多得让他每年捐出 2 亿美元给慈善事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in the early 2000s, he was donating like $700 million a year.
zh: 我记得在 2000 年代初，他每年捐赠大约 7 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think he's given something like over $10 billion a year to like philanthropic, different like charities and philanthropic endeavors that he was interested in.
zh: 我记得他每年捐赠超过 100 亿美元给他感兴趣的各种慈善和公益事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the same time, scattered throughout the book, he's got these just like very, again, unapologetically extreme perspectives.
zh: 与此同时，散布在全书中的，是他那些非常、再次强调，毫不掩饰地极端的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is one of my favorite.
zh: 这是我最喜欢的之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, since Bloomberg was always up against companies many times our size, we had to enter each commercial fight with an advantage.
zh: 他说，由于 Bloomberg 一直以来面对的都是规模是我们许多倍的公司，我们必须带着优势进入每一场商业战斗。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't believe that business battles should ever be even.
zh: 我不相信商业战斗应该是势均力敌的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Bloomberg, we do not want fair fights.
zh: 在 Bloomberg,我们不想要公平的战斗。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to go into contests with an advantage.
zh: 我们要带着优势进入每一场较量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this made me think of when I got to this section, Jeff Bezos said something that's very similar.
zh: 这让我想到，当我读到这一节时，Jeff Bezos 说过非常类似的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I asked Sage about this.
zh: 所以我问了 Sage 这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I asked, like, what did Jeff Bezos say about not wanting to fight a competitor as strong as you are?
zh: 我问，Jeff Bezos 关于不想与和自己一样强的竞争对手战斗说过什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it pulled a quote from one of his past episodes.
zh: 它从他的某一期过往节目里拉出了一段引言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it says, when it comes to competition, this is Jeff Bezos now, when it comes to competition, being one of the best is not good enough.
zh: 上面说，说到竞争，现在是 Jeff Bezos 在说，说到竞争，成为最好的之一是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you really want to plan for a future in which you might have to fight with somebody who is just as good as you are?
zh: 你真的想规划一个你可能不得不与和你一样强的人战斗的未来吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't.
zh: 我不想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bloomberg is saying the exact same thing.
zh: Bloomberg 说的完全是同一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to go into all these contests with an unfair advantage.
zh: 我们要带着不公平的优势进入所有这些较量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do not believe that business battles should be even.
zh: 我不相信商业战斗应该是势均力敌的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he talks about the importance of persistence, of resourcefulness.
zh: 然后他谈到坚持的重要性，以及随机应变的重要性。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, most fortunes are built by entrepreneurs who started with nothing and generally got fired once or twice in their careers.
zh: 他说，大多数财富都是由从一无所有开始、并且在职业生涯中通常被解雇过一两次的创业者创造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And throughout history, the vast majority of great writers, artists, musicians, dancers, and athletes have come from the less financially secure families.
zh: 而纵观历史，绝大多数伟大的作家、艺术家、音乐家、舞蹈家和运动员都来自经济上不太宽裕的家庭。

speaker: Unknown
en: The CEOs of many Fortune 500 companies went to a state university rather than an Ivy League school.
zh: 许多财富 500 强公司的 CEO 上的是州立大学，而不是常春藤盟校。

speaker: Unknown
en: The rewards almost always go to those who outwork the others.
zh: 回报几乎总是属于那些比别人更勤奋工作的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The time you put in is the single most important controllable variable determining your future.
zh: 你投入的时间是决定你未来的唯一最重要的可控变量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Communists tried to eliminate any form of meritocracy for 70 years, and in addition to wrecking their economies, they starved millions of people to death in the process.
zh: 共产主义者试图消灭任何形式的精英管理体制，持续了70年，结果不仅摧毁了他们的经济，还在这个过程中饿死了数百万人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally, he has some great advice for the future generations of entrepreneurs.
zh: 最后，他给未来的创业者们提了一些很好的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Periodically, while surrounded by the fruits of our success, the profits, the power, the notoriety, I get frustrated and dream of starting again.
zh: 起初简单的东西，随着时间推移变得复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: But something stops me.
zh: 但总有什么东西阻止了我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Perhaps I'm too old.
zh: 也许我太老了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Perhaps I'm afraid it was all luck.
zh: 也许我害怕那一切全是运气。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or maybe deep down inside, I really do like the trappings that have accumulated.
zh: 又或者，在内心深处，我真的很喜欢这些累积起来的排场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nevertheless, when I find we have to clear it with legal, or had a meeting just to keep others in the loop, or are justifying staff versus producers, I want to scream.
zh: 然而，当我发现我们必须通过法务的审查，或者开会只是为了知会其他人，或者为了员工人数与实际产出做辩护时，我想尖叫。

speaker: Unknown
en: We used to have the Nike motto attitude.
zh: 我们曾经抱着 Nike 那句口号的态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just did it.
zh: 我们就是干了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now there's a why we can't lurking in the background.
zh: 现在却有一个「为什么不行」潜伏在幕后。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keeping it from coming out while we grow is our number one management focus today.
zh: 在我们成长的过程中阻止它冒出来，是我们今天的第一管理重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: What started simple with time has become complex.
zh: 最初简单的东西随着时间变得复杂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: A single straightforward policy has picked up exception after exception over time.
zh: 一项原本简单直接的政策，随着时间推移被加上一个又一个例外。

speaker: Unknown
en: Products have grown to overlap.
zh: 产品已经发展到相互重叠。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one's got an excuse, but everyone's got a reason.
zh: 没有人找借口，但每个人都有理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is maddening.
zh: 这令人抓狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why not just quit then?
zh: 那为什么不干脆放弃呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Chuck it all.
zh: 全都甩掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sell the business.
zh: 卖掉公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take the money and run.
zh: 拿着钱走人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why not cash in?
zh: 为什么不变现？

speaker: Unknown
en: Play it conservative.
zh: 保守行事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Relax.
zh: 放松一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Real entrepreneurs never do, and I haven't either.
zh: 真正的创业者从不这样做，我也从未这样做过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Real builders are so focused and dedicated they'd have a nervous breakdown after two weeks of sitting around.
zh: 真正的建设者非常专注和投入，闲坐两周他们就会精神崩溃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their challenge, even their reason for living, would be gone.
zh: 他们的挑战，甚至他们活下去的理由，都会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why swap fun, influence, challenge, and more money than you could ever spend for only a multiple of more money than you can ever spend?
zh: 为什么要用乐趣、影响力、挑战，以及多得永远花不完的钱，去换只是数倍于多得永远花不完的钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't think of anything better than my current situation.
zh: 我想不出有什么比我现在的情况更好的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And why would I take the company public?
zh: 那我为什么要把公司上市？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would I have to answer to more partners, stockholders, and security and analysts?
zh: 为什么我要向更多的合伙人、股东、证券和分析师负责？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know why the investment bankers want me to issue stock, but why would we want to do it?
zh: 我知道投资银行家为什么想让我发行股票，但我们为什么想这么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going in the other direction.
zh: 我们正在朝相反的方向走。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've already bought back Merrill's 30% investment in our company, the first 10% for $200 million in 1996, and the second 20% for $4.5 billion in 2008.
zh: 我们已经回购了 Merrill 在我们公司的30%投资，第一个10%在1996年以2亿美元回购，第二个20%在2008年以45亿美元回购。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not a bad return on their original investment of about $30 million.
zh: 相对于他们最初约3000万美元的投资，这回报不算差。

speaker: Unknown
en: So why not sell?
zh: 那为什么不卖掉呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: No thanks.
zh: 不必了，谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Answering to no one is the ultimate situation.
zh: 不必向任何人负责是终极的境地。

speaker: Unknown
en: So back on the treadmill, ratchet up the risk, enter a new medium, start another project, improve, develop, expand, go.
zh: 所以回到跑步机上，加大风险，进入一个新领域，启动另一个项目，改进、开发、扩张、前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is where I'll leave it for the full story.
zh: 关于完整的故事，我就讲到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I highly recommend reading the book.
zh: 我强烈推荐读这本书。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is 433 books down, 1,000 to go.
zh: 那就是已经读完433本书，还有1000本要去读。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll talk to you again soon.
zh: 我们很快会再聊。
